_comment: 🔴 /assets/ IS EXCLUDED FROM THE SPA FALLBACK ON PURPOSE (2026-09-21).
Without the exclusion this rewrite answered a MISSING hashed chunk with
index.html — HTTP 200, content-type text/html — so a page that lazy-loaded
a chunk from the build it started on got markup where it expected a
module. Measured on prod: /assets/web-BITZqWmZ.js (previous build) came
back 200 text/html while the current one came back application/javascript.
That is the mechanism behind the iPhone reports this repo chased for days:
'Unexpected token <' surfacing as stockfish-error and lichess-error
TypeError: Load failed, with NOTHING anywhere naming a 404. It is also why
it took a device to find — no server log records an error, because the
server thinks it served a page successfully.
And every deploy creates the situation: vite.config.ts bakes Date.now()
into __BUILD_ID__, so every build renames every chunk, docs-only pushes
included.
A 404 is the honest answer and the useful one. It is detectable by the app,
by the service worker, and by an audit; HTML-pretending-to-be-JS is
detectable by none of them without a content-type check nobody thinks to
write. EXISTING assets are unaffected — Vercel serves a matching static
file before consulting rewrites, so this only changes what happens when
the file is genuinely gone.
Do NOT 'fix' a 404 on /assets/ by restoring the fallback. The 404 IS the
fix; a chunk that is not there should say so.
